properties.name: WHAT WORKED (2026-10-02, 0.77.0): through `--call`, a write missing an argument is refused and names it. A deserializer-level miss exits 2, and a constructor's missing create-time content exits 1 with every missing field listed at once. Do not regress it; its nested-field case is the defect recorded beside it
properties.statement:
From art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, measured table row "a write with a missing argument | exit 2; the message names the missing argument".

Re-measured by triage agent B on 0.77.0, scratch store:
- A required field missing at deserialisation exits 2 and names the tool and the field (add_decision `evidence`, set_artifact_checksums `disposition`).
- A constructor's create-time content exits 1 (refusal on stderr) and names ALL of it in one go: add_epoch "Also missing: epoch_type"; add_decision with only an id names `name` and `decision`.
So "exit 2" holds for the deserializer path only. An instructions file that tells an agent "exit 2 means missing argument" would misread the exit-1 constructor case. Both are clear.

THE PART THAT DID NOT WORK is recorded separately: for a field inside an array item the message falsely says the schema "publishes no description" (fact:root-cause-a-missing-nested-field-refusal-says-the-schema-publishes-no-description-when-it-does-2026-10-02).
